name: Ulysses S. Grant
kicker: Union general who won the Civil War · 18th U.S. President
briefing: Ulysses S. Grant failed as a farmer and businessman before the Civil War, but once the fighting began he won a string of key victories in the West, including the capture of Vicksburg. Abraham Lincoln put him in charge of all Union armies, and in April 1865 Robert E. Lee surrendered to him at Appomattox Court House. Grant then served two terms as the 18th president, and while dying of cancer he wrote memoirs that became a best seller.

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: This man was born Hiram in Point Pleasant, Ohio, in 1822, but Congressman Thomas Hamer wrote down the wrong name when nominating him to West Point, giving him a new middle initial. His classmates there nicknamed him “Sam.”
tossups.r: He later fought in the Mexican-American War. For 10 points, name this Union general who accepted Robert E. Lee’s surrender and became the 18th president.

tossups.p: In the 1850s, this man built a log house he called “Hardscrabble” on a farm near St. Louis and sold firewood on the city’s streets. When a war began in 1861, he was working as a clerk in his family’s leather goods store in Galena, Illinois.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this man who rose to command all Union armies in the Civil War.

tossups.p: In his memoirs, this general called the Mexican-American War, in which he had fought as a young officer, one of the most unjust wars ever waged by a stronger nation against a weaker one. In that war, he served as his regiment’s quartermaster, keeping its soldiers supplied.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Union general who later served two terms as president, from 1869 to 1877.

tossups.p: In February 1862, this general told his old friend Simon Bolivar Buckner that “no terms except an unconditional and immediate surrender” would be accepted at Fort Donelson in Tennessee. Days earlier, this general had captured nearby Fort Henry.
tossups.r: Newspapers joked that his initials stood for “Unconditional Surrender.” For 10 points, name this Union general and later president.

tossups.p: In April 1862, Albert Sidney Johnston’s Confederates surprised this general’s army near Pittsburg Landing, Tennessee, but Johnston was killed, and reinforcements under Don Carlos Buell helped this general win on the second day. That battle was named for a small log church.
tossups.r: That battle was Shiloh. For 10 points, name this Union general who later captured Vicksburg.

tossups.p: Benjamin Grierson’s cavalry raid through Mississippi distracted Confederate defenders while this general marched his army south and crossed the Mississippi River below his target in 1863. After a siege of more than six weeks, John C. Pemberton surrendered that city to him.
tossups.r: That city was Vicksburg, which fell on July 4, 1863. For 10 points, name this Union general.

tossups.p: In November 1863, this general broke the siege of Chattanooga, Tennessee, after Union troops won the Battle of Lookout Mountain and then charged up Missionary Ridge. A few months later, Congress revived the rank of lieutenant general so that he could be promoted.
tossups.r: Abraham Lincoln then put him in charge of all Union armies. For 10 points, name this general who later became the 18th president.

tossups.p: During fighting at Spotsylvania Court House in May 1864, this general wrote, “I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer.” His Overland Campaign also included the Battle of the Wilderness and a failed assault at Cold Harbor.
tossups.r: That campaign wore down Lee’s army in Virginia. For 10 points, name this Union general who became the 18th president.

tossups.p: Ely Parker, a Seneca officer on this general’s staff, wrote out the final copy of the surrender terms that this general offered in Wilmer McLean’s parlor in April 1865. Those generous terms let Confederate soldiers go home and take their own horses with them.
tossups.r: Robert E. Lee surrendered to him at Appomattox Court House. For 10 points, name this Union general.

tossups.p: In January 1868, this general angered President Andrew Johnson by giving up his job as acting Secretary of War so that Edwin Stanton could return to the office. Months later, the Republicans nominated this general for president, and he ran with the slogan “Let us have peace.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this man who won the 1868 election and became the 18th president.

tossups.p: On September 24, 1869, a day called Black Friday, gold prices crashed after this president ordered the Treasury to sell gold, ruining a plan by Jay Gould and James Fisk to corner the market. This president’s brother-in-law, Abel Corbin, had been part of their scheme.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 18th president, whose two terms also saw the Whiskey Ring scandal.

tossups.p: Under this president, Secretary of State Hamilton Fish negotiated the Treaty of Washington with Britain in 1871. An international panel in Geneva then ordered Britain to pay $15.5 million for damage done by the _Alabama_ and other British-built Confederate raiders.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this president from 1869 to 1877, who had earlier commanded the Union armies.

tossups.p: In 1871, this president used new Enforcement Acts to send troops and federal prosecutors against the Ku Klux Klan, even suspending habeas corpus [“HAY-bee-us KOR-pus”] in nine South Carolina counties. The Department of Justice, created in 1870 during his first term, led many of those prosecutions.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 18th president, who had commanded the Union armies at the end of the Civil War.

tossups.p: In 1872, this president signed the law creating Yellowstone, the world’s first national park. That same year, he won reelection over Horace Greeley, a newspaper editor who died before the Electoral College voted.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 18th president, who had led the Union armies to victory in the Civil War.

tossups.p: While dying of throat cancer at Mount McGregor, New York, this man raced to finish his memoirs, which Mark Twain’s publishing company sold with huge success to support his family. He and his wife, Julia, lie in Manhattan’s Riverside Park, in the largest mausoleum in North America.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Civil War general and 18th president, whose face is on the $50 bill.

clues.t: Commanding general of all Union armies, who led the North to victory in the Civil War
Accepted Robert E. Lee’s surrender at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, on April 9, 1865
18th President of the United States (1869–1877), a Republican
His face is on the fifty-dollar ($50) bill
Captured Vicksburg, Mississippi, after a siege (July 4, 1863), giving the Union control of the Mississippi River
Demanded “unconditional and immediate surrender” from Simon Bolivar Buckner at Fort Donelson (1862); people joked his initials meant “Unconditional Surrender”
Survived a surprise attack at Shiloh, Tennessee (April 1862), and won on the second day
Graduated from West Point (1843) and fought in the Mexican-American War
As president, enforced Reconstruction and used troops and federal courts against the Ku Klux Klan (1871)
Scandals during his presidency included the Whiskey Ring and Crédit Mobilier
Wrote his _Personal Memoirs_ while dying of throat cancer; Mark Twain’s company published them (1885)
Signed the 1872 law creating Yellowstone, the first national park
Promoted to lieutenant general in 1864 and given command of all Union armies
Fought Lee in the 1864 Overland Campaign (the Wilderness, Spotsylvania, Cold Harbor), then besieged Petersburg
Born Hiram (1822, Point Pleasant, Ohio); Congressman Thomas Hamer’s mistake on his West Point nomination changed his name
In the 1850s, farmed at “Hardscrabble” near St. Louis; in 1861 he was clerking in the family leather store in Galena, Illinois
His memoirs called the Mexican-American War one of the most unjust wars ever waged by a stronger nation against a weaker one
At Spotsylvania (1864): “I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer”
Ely Parker, a Seneca on his staff, wrote out the surrender terms; Parker later became the first Native American Commissioner of Indian Affairs
Lee surrendered in Wilmer McLean’s parlor; the terms let Confederate soldiers go home with their own horses
Broke the siege of Chattanooga (November 1863) with wins at Lookout Mountain and Missionary Ridge
As acting Secretary of War, he angered Andrew Johnson by giving the office back to Edwin Stanton (1868)
Won in 1868 with the slogan “Let us have peace”; in 1872 he beat Horace Greeley, who died before the electoral vote
Black Friday (1869): Jay Gould and James Fisk tried to corner the gold market until his Treasury sold gold
The Department of Justice was created in 1870, during his first term; he suspended habeas corpus in nine South Carolina counties to fight the Klan
Secretary of State Hamilton Fish’s Treaty of Washington (1871) settled the Alabama Claims; Britain paid $15.5 million
Buried in New York City’s Riverside Park, in the largest mausoleum in North America

trap.title: Which Union general?
trap.body: Tossups about this man are crowded with other Civil War names. Robert E. Lee surrendered to him at Appomattox, William Tecumseh Sherman was his most trusted general and marched through Georgia, George McClellan led the Union army early in the war, and George Meade won at Gettysburg. Blurting out a name you just heard in the question is the fastest way to lose this tossup.
trap.fix: Grant clues: Fort Donelson’s “unconditional surrender,” Shiloh, Vicksburg, Appomattox, the 18th presidency, and memoirs published by Mark Twain. Plain “Grant” is enough, but “Ulysses” alone is not.
trap.line: Real answer line: Ulysses S. Grant (or Hiram Ulysses Grant)
